In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1) the staging system for prostate cancer is inadequate, (2) the grading system for prostate cancer needs improvement, (3) a high percentage of patients with clinically localized prostate cancer have occult metastatic disease at the time of radical prostatectomy, (4) the pathologic grade is more important than the stage in determining the risk of persistent or recurrence disease, and (5) radiation therapy is a safe and effective adjuvant treatment for patients with high-grade prostate cancer.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the clinical stage, the grade, and the extent of the tumor as determined by needle biopsy are not reliable criteria for predicting the outcome in patients treated for prostate carcinoma by radical prostatectomv.

the pathologic staging of prostate cancer is not as reliable as we had thought and that postoperative irradiation is an effective treatment modality for patients at high risk after radical prostatectomv.

the clinical stage of prostate cancer is often understaged and that the pathologic grade often is underestimated.
